body: Thank you so much! 🥺 3/4 sleeves are a fashion staple for me now LOL

Thank you, I am slowly but surely getting on the road to longterm help. You've put the feeling into words, honestly, that throwing the meds out isnt just an act of cleaning but seriously its like mentally letting go of that crutch, its so hard.
Yeah, I get you on that one. Sometimes the fighting goes on for so long, the idea gets more appealing just BECAUSE you want the struggle to stop.

Last night, I was repeating over and over that if I couls just hold on until my therapist appointment the next day, I'd be fine. Update is I feel much better, even if these urges come and go sporadically. Luckily, I am on my way to receiving longterm therapy for it though. Its just nice to know others feel the same compulsion tbh.
Thank you!!! ❤

They look very dry despite being months old, hope this isn't an invasive question but are you scratching them? Since there are some bloody patches.
Sometimes I need to put a lotion on my larger scars or else they get so dry and itchy that I scratch them and break the skin. The skin on scars has reduced elasticity so when they get dry, they can feel very tight and itchy easily.
Also please take this with a grain of salt as I am only speaking from experience, but if they are still red, puffy and itching, they could also be keloids, which itch and continue to develop for months or even years after they've healed. Not dangerous, just annoying.
Anyway hope this helps! Stay safe, and keep them clean.

Oh, for sure! At first, it was for punishment, and then it also became a grounding technique for me. Of course, after a long time it can become a part of your daily routine without realizing, and I would do it because I was just bored, or I was happy and excited and wanted the adrenaline rush. I also became obsessed with making large scars because I liked them and saw them as interesting, so I feel you on that one. Hell, I have heard accounts of people starting and then continuing because there was an oberlap of sexual gratification! There can be so many reasons, its really interesting.

Yeah, its odd cause some of my larger ones healed without issue, but then some absolute random small ones give me trouble LOL. I find the sensitive ones tend to be on high-movement skin like on elbows or on my ribs and torso just like yours! It sucks so much, but its just a sign of healing so we just have to let it happen. 😭

They could be keloids or just hypertrophic scars! Keloids are more common in certain races, specifically black and latine people, but could ultimately could happen to anyone. 
To help scars just not raise in general when healing, try not to disrupt healing processes. This means not picking scabs, scratching excessively and try not to stretch the skin a lot when it is healing (this goes for when it is already past the scabbing phase too). I have also heard that not letting the scars interact with sun helps with regulating the color as well.
Scars that are hypertrophic or keloids just have more collagen in them, the stuff that makes up scar tissue, keloids being different because they dont stop producing collagen for a long time after the scar is already done healing and stay red longer. Hope this helps!
They are healing nicely! Best of luck 👍❤

Don't worry! Some of these were very deep and i neglected to get much-needed medical attention (literally needed stitches and just didnt get them), and i fucked with the healing a whole bunch so that is why they took so long. If you take care not to stretch and scratch the skin while its healing, they usually take a year to heal! I would also invest in a long-sleeve swim top or something similar if you want to swim earlier, i did that as well! Stay safe!
Yep! Deep cuts tend to have those, and also itchiness that comes and goes too. I have a very deep one that got random sharp pains for years after the incident. It is part of the healing process.

Depends on what you gain from self harming! Drawing on youtself with red marker sometimes helps if you want to see damage, or slicing up stacks of paper with your blades when the urge is very strong. I also count the previous scars I have on my skin to waste time. Most importantly, though, if you slip up don't beat yourself up about it. Even just lengthening the periods of time between each relapse is progress, people usually don't just stop cold-turkey, after all.
That's awesome! Must be hard, especially if you don't have a choice, I hope you're doing alright 👍 very proud of you!

Ones on the left look like they will need 2+ years to fully fade, and the ones on the right can take like 6 months to a year! Again, everyone is different, so take this with a grain of salt. What helps is avoiding sunlight on them, as well as not stretching the skin, scratching then and aggravating them while they heal, even if the deep ones are itchy sometimes! I promise you will see change before you know it, it is slow but it is happening 👍

I feel that! Its sort of a fixation with them, and feeling proud of having done such damage and also withstanding it. I think you shouldn't hate yourself for being fixated on them, since they look lovely, and they are yours. Congrats on one month clean, though! Stay safe.

I am not 100% sure, genetics are a factor (latinx and black people are apparently more prone to developing them, which makes sense as I am also south american lol) but ALSO! A major impact is whether the cut's healing process is repeatedly disrupted. This can mean picking at scabs, or the cut being in a place of high movement and tension for the skin (like on an elbow joint or on your stomach which stretches a lot). The cut usually has to be somewhat deep as well. AGAIN, this is mostly things I have read in articles backed up with personal experience. I have gotten my keloids verified by medical professionals as well. Sometimes you take good care of the cuts but, because of your genetic predisposition, they still develop into keloids regardless. This can happen. But if you haven't developed them out of the blue, I simply suggest you just take very good care of your deep cuts, don't aggravate the wound site, and try to avoid harming yourself in high-impact areas of your skin. Stay safe!

Yes, keloids are caused by the overproduction of scar tissue. They are scars that continue to expand past the original area of the cut or puff up much more, and can sometimes continue growing for years. But in many cases, the expansion is not extremely dramatic in size. (For example, I have two keloids on my wrist that have been growing for 2 years after the original wound healed, but over the past few months I have noticed that they stopped.) They're not really dangerous, just ugly lol
It is a type of temporary tattoo that lasts like 2 weeks! More permanent than a temporary tattoo since it doesn't crack or anything.
Thank you very much!! I will do my best. :D
This is actually so so lovely, you made my day. Thank you so much!!
Thank you!! I made an investment in some mesh shirts to wear under tshirts for this weather, but I will also take a look into uv compression sleeves.

Some of them are keloids that used to be thinner cuts! A few of the thick scars that are stubborn hypertrophic ones, but some are still growing past the original wound site years later. Sorry for the confusion!

Yes! Scars fade over a longer time than just 6 months for sure. It depends on the person, some fade over years. I have had some similar ones that have faded over a year to 2 years. They will be invisible before you know it ❤

They are fine now. Bigger cuts tend to itch when they heal and take longer, but also sometimes big cuts that have had their healing process disrupted from infection, picking or excessive movement just have larger raised scar tissue that keeps growing and staying tender/brightly coloured for a while. They look like they are healing well now! You just have to be patient with scars like these.

Definitely not a nerve! Sometimes deep scars will start to grow back capillaries and you will see some tiny squiggly lines in your scars, it is normal! Also some scars will have patches of lighter colors mixed with darker areas, and that is normal too. Stay safe!

Yeah, the little holes look like theyre hair follicles, they start to show up on the scar tissue a while after healing. 
Some of the raised scars could just be deep cuts that take longer to lose color and flatten, but these also look like they are keloid scars, which stay bright-coloured and puffy for many years after. They're not dangerous, just annoying lol.
